press_wire.title: Manzambi starts for first time as Villa make four changes
Gomes starts at Spurs
press_wire.summary: Fixtures Tottenham Hotspur Vs. Aston Villa - Sat, Sep 19 2026, 12:30 João Gomes returned to Aston Villa’s starting XI for Saturday’s Premier League clash at Tottenham Hotspur while there was also a full debut for Johan Manzambi. Midfielder Gomes completed his three-match suspension having been sent off at Brighton & Hove Albion on the opening weekend of the season. He returned to Villa’s line-up for the lunchtime kick-off in the capital, as fit-again Manzambi also made his first start for the club following two substitute appearances. In total, Unai Emery made seven changes from Wednesday’s Carabao Cup triumph at Coventry City. Zion Suzuki, Victor Lindelöf, Boubacar Kamara, Emi Buendía and Nicolas Jackson also returned to face Spurs. Goalkeeper James Wright was named among the substitutes, alongside Matty Cash and Taylor Harwood-Bellis for the encounter at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

press_wire.title: Moyes' Programme Notes For Ipswich Test
press_wire.summary: Welcome back to Hill Dickinson Stadium for our fifth Premier League fixture of the season. Our last time out here in the Premier League saw us come away with a last-minute point against Manchester United. On the day we felt we were worthy of at least a draw and that we had done enough to justify getting something from the game. The goal which earned us that point, from Ainsley Maitland-Niles, was a magnificent strike and hopefully representative of the kind of quality we will see from Everton players in this stadium many times in the future. It was also great to see Tyrique George score his first goal for the Club in spectacular fashion. While we came away perhaps a little disappointed we didn’t win, we were also happy to secure a point so late in the game. The performances and attitude of the players helped generate a great atmosphere in the stadium throughout the afternoon. There was another great turnout on Wednesday when we got the job done against Wolves in the Carabao Cup, which earned a home tie in the next round against Newcastle United. For long periods of the match we dominated and eventually got the goal we deserved in the end. We were pleased with lots of aspects of our game, happy to see ourselves through to the last 16 of the competition and pleased we received another home draw in the fourth round. After today’s game we will have a three-week international break. We’re used to international breaks early in the season but this time it’s unusual to have such a long gap between Premier League fixtures. It will cause a few problems for many clubs in that some will have very few players left behind to form training groups. The most important thing for us is that, with players facing four games in three weeks with their international teams, our players do not pick up any injuries while they are away. It is a privilege for our players to represent their countries and we hope we continue to have players called up, but equally I hope they all return safe, well and in good condition. We have plans for the players who are not away, to train, have some rest time and possibly have a game to keep them in as good a condition as possible and ready for when we return to action at Hull City. Finally, I would like to welcome Gary O’Neil and his Ipswich team and staff here today. It’s good to see Ipswich Town back in the Premier League. They have had some wonderful teams throughout their history. Some of you will remember the magnificent side they had under Bobby Robson, which featured some amazing players like Paul Mariner, Alan Brazil and John Wark. They have a great history and it’s good to see them back in the top division. Today is another difficult test and nothing can be taken for granted in this league. We want to continue building momentum and with your support behind us we hope to gain another valuable three points today. Enjoy the game. David

press_wire.title: REDS OVERCOME WEST BROM ON THE ROAD
press_wire.summary: Nottingham Forest’s B Team saw out a well-earned 3-1 victory against West Bromwich Albion in the Premier League 2 on Friday night. The Forest defence weathered the initial storm from the Baggies, preventing the home side from having any clear-cut chances in the early stages. An ill-timed tackle saw Forest concede a penalty; however, Keehan Willows superbly pushed the spot kick onto the bottom-left post, and the backline was there to clear the danger. Just minutes later, Matty Orr’s well-timed header was narrowly tipped over the crossbar by Ben Cisse in the West Brom net, igniting the momentum back into the Reds. Forest took a well-deserved lead through a low-driven shot by Shakur Samuels, which nestled neatly into the bottom-right corner. Getting his brace for the evening, Samuels blasted the ball into the roof of the net yet again, sending the young Reds into the break with a two-goal advantage. Shortly after the break, West Brom’s Cole Dexter pulled one back for the home side, with a shot which Willows was unable to do anything about. However, the young Reds responded exceptionally well, knocking on the door yet again, as Fuad Smith’s right-footed effort rattled the post. Dylan Malicheff’s choice of substitutions was spot on, as, following his introduction, Kayne Bradshaw sealed the result for the team, firing home from the edge of the penalty area. The team remained focused until the final whistle, ensuring no further threat to the three points collected on the road. Forest will turn their attention to Tuesday’s EFL Trophy clash, travelling to the Pirelli Stadium, where Burton Albion await.

press_wire.title: London calling as Villa visit Spurs
press_wire.summary: Fixtures Tottenham Hotspur Vs. Aston Villa - Sat, Sep 19 2026, 12:30 Aston Villa look to claim their first victory of the Premier League season on Saturday, when visiting Tottenham Hotspur. Unai Emery takes his team to North London for the day’s lunchtime kick-off (12.30pm), with just a point to their name thus far. The Villans will, however, be buoyed by wins in the UEFA Champions League and Carabao Cup over Club Brugge and Coventry City respectively, the latter in midweek meaning they will be aiming for back-to-back triumphs when visiting the capital. Like the Villans, Spurs have endured a far-from-ideal start to the league campaign, sitting just two places above their visitors with one point more, as they remain searching for their first goal of the season. Roberto De Zerbi’s side were knocked out of the Carabao Cup at the third-round stage on Tuesday, losing 3-1 away at Liverpool after a 5-1 win at home to Charlton Athletic in round two. Stats None of the last 22 Premier League meetings between Spurs (15 wins) and Villa (7) have been drawn. Spurs have lost five of the last eight, more than they had in their previous 29 against the Villans (W18 D7 L4). Villa have won four of their last six Premier League away games against Spurs (L2), more than they had in their previous 21 visits (W3 D5 L13). Tottenham have drawn 0-0 in each of their last two Premier League games, as many times as in their previous 181 matches in the competition; the last side to record three successive goalless draws in the competition was West Ham United in December 2015, with Spurs last doing so in January/February 2001 under George Graham (run of 4). Only in 1919/20 (first 7), 1964/65 (7) and 2025/26 (5) have Villa failed to win any of their opening five matches of a top-flight league season (D1 L3 so far). After winning each of his first three encounters with Spurs’ Roberto De Zerbi, Villa boss Unai Emery has lost each of the last two meetings, including a 2-1 reverse at Villa Park in May. Tottenham (3.45) and Villa (3.39) rank 19th and 20th in the Premier League so far this season for expected goals. Meanwhile, Spurs are bottom for xG per shot (0.07), and only Hull City (47) have had fewer touches in the opposition’s box than Villa (62). Alysson’s goal against Nottingham Forest was Villa’s 34th Premier League goal via a substitute since the start of 2023/24. Only Brighton (40) and Arsenal (36) have scored more in that time, with two of Villa’s three goals against Spurs last season coming via subs. Villa (30.5%) and Spurs (28.7%) rank fifth and seventh in the Premier League this season for the proportion of their attacking touches coming in the middle third, while 58.3% of Villa’s chances have come through the middle third, the highest proportion of any side. Of the six players to complete 9+ take-ons in the Premier League so far this season, three play for Tottenham in Mathys Tel (10/22), Omar Marmoush (9/17) and Sávio (9/23). Last time out against Everton, Sávio became the first player this season to complete four take-ons and create four chances from open play. Villa’s Emi Buendía has been involved in four Premier League goals against Tottenham (3 goals, 1 assist), his most against a single side in the competition – he could become the third visiting player to score in three successive league trips to the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, after Eberechi Eze and Bryan Mbeumo. The Last Meeting The last meeting between these two sides was one to forget from a Villa standpoint, as they went down 2-1 at home to Spurs towards the end of last season. A scintillating start from the visitors at Villa Park saw them go two goals up inside the opening 25 minutes. Conor Gallagher lashed home from distance before Richarlison nodded home Mathys Tel’s cross – after João Pahlinha had struck Emi Martínez’s post. Emi Buendía flicked a looping header into the far corner in front of The Holte End six minutes into added time, but it was too late to save the Villans from falling to defeat. Team News Unai Emery revealed at his pre-match press conference that Marco Bizot had joined Villa’s growing injury list, but João Gomes is fit to feature, having completed his suspension. Matty Cash could return having not featured since the stalemate at Hull City, but Pau Torres, Ian Maatsen, Leon Goretzka, Brian Madjo, Amadou Onana and Modou Kéba Cissé remain sidelined. For Spurs, Roberto De Zerbi revealed all of Pedro Porro, Marcus Maddison and Sandro Tonali would be fit enough to feature for his side. The hosts are, however, without Xavi Simons, Dejan Kulusevski, Mykhailo Mudryk and Wilson Odobert, who all remain sidelined through injury. Managers' Pre-Match Thoughts “Tomorrow is a huge challenge for us, how we are going to respond, how we are going to play as well in our structure, being compact and feeling confidence to play, and facing them as well in a difficult match.” - Unai Emery “They have one of the best coaches in the world. Their style is clear, even though they’ve changed many players. So, it’s a tough game for us. I think it’s a tough game also for them.” - Roberto De Zerbi
